title: Ganjin's sixth voyage to Japan, 748–754
summary: The Chinese monk Ganjin tried about six times between 743 and 754 to reach Japan. The fifth try, from Yangzhou in 748, was blown past the Zhoushan islands to Hainan. In autumn 753, blind, he boarded a Japanese embassy ship and landed in Kyushu on 20 December. He reached Nara in spring 754.

legs.source: Jianzhen (Wikipedia): the fifth attempt left Yangzhou, reached the Zhoushan Archipelago and was blown off course to Hainan
legs.note: Only the fifth attempt is drawn; the other attempts are not dated or placed in the source. The mouth of the Yangtze stands for Yangzhou, which lies up the river.

legs.source: Jianzhen (Wikipedia): boarded a Japanese emissary ship in autumn 753, landed at Kagoshima on 20 December; the way between is not in the source
legs.note: Usually drawn south of the line the earlier embassies took, by the Ryukyu islands; the source does not name the course.

legs.source: Jianzhen (Wikipedia): reached Nara in spring 754; the road is not in the source
legs.note: A straight editorial line; he travelled by the usual ways of the time, partly by water.

events.label: Ganjin sets out from Yangzhou
events.text: The fifth attempt left Yangzhou in the summer of 748. The ship was blown off course past the Zhoushan islands to Hainan, and he returned overland to Yangzhou.

events.label: Landfall at Kagoshima
events.text: He landed in Kyushu on 20 December 753.

events.label: Welcomed at Nara
events.text: He presided over Tōdai-ji; in 759 he retired to western Nara and founded Tōshōdai-ji.
